passage: When we listen to music, our brain quietly builds a model of the steady pulse it expects to hear.
This internal model lets us notice the exact moment a performer departs from that pulse.
The same thing happens with melody: we hold a mental picture of the tune so that we can recognize when a musician bends it.
Sensing the beat and predicting when it will fall is therefore a core source of musical feeling.
Music reaches us emotionally precisely by violating, in a systematic way, the expectations it has set up.
Such violations may appear in pitch, in rhythm, in tempo, or elsewhere, but appear they must.
Sound that is organized yet contains no surprise feels emotionally flat and mechanical.
Too much order is still music in a strict sense, but it is music nobody cares to hear.
choices: how repeated listening helps people memorize complex melodies
why a steady, unchanging rhythm is the highest goal of music
how music stirs emotion by violating the patterns our brain expects
how musicians are trained to keep perfect time during a performance
why some listeners prefer organized music to improvised music

theme.distractor_ko: ①암기, ②변함없는 리듬 예찬, ④박자 훈련, ⑤취향 비교는 본문 초점이 아니다.

summary.summary_template: Music stirs emotion when a musician deliberately __(B)__ the very patterns that the brain has come to __(A)__; sound that is merely organized, with nothing unexpected, leaves us emotionally flat.
summary.explanation_ko: 뇌는 일정한 박자·멜로디의 패턴을 (A)anticipate(예상)하고, 음악가가 그 패턴을 (B)break(깨뜨릴=systematic violations) 때 감정이 생긴다. ③ anticipate / breaks 가 정답.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)는 예상하다(anticipate), (B)는 깨뜨리다(breaks)여야 한다. follows·preserves·repeats는 '위반'의 반대이고, ignore·distrust·forget은 뇌가 패턴을 모델링한다는 본문과 어긋난다.

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 본문 내용을 바탕으로 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 한 단어씩 쓰시오. (본문의 표현을 그대로 옮기지 않아도 됨)
